workbook.description: These 2 files contain current packaging waste data, aggregated from accredited reprocessor and exporter reports under extended producer responsibility (EPR) for packaging.
workbook.heading: Download aggregated data

accreditations.nation: A report is only counted if the accreditation it relates to is currently approved or suspended. Where an accreditation has been cancelled, it counts neither as a submission nor as a non-submission for the relevant period. Any tonnage associated with a cancelled accreditation will remain in the waste balance so as not to distort the overall picture of packaging waste reprocessing and export.
accreditations.uk: A report counts only if the accreditation it was submitted for is currently approved or suspended. Where an accreditation has been cancelled, it counts neither as a submission nor as a non-submission for the relevant period. Any tonnage associated with a cancelled accreditation will remain in the waste balance so as not to distort the overall picture of packaging waste reprocessing and export.

calculation.average: Operators report notes issued ‘free of charge’ separately, and that tonnage is not included. Revenue and tonnage are each added up across all operators, then total revenue is divided by total tonnage to give the average price of each tonne. Where no tonnage was issued, the average is 0.
calculation.heading: How the tables are compiled
calculation.revenue: Revenue is what operators reported as received, or are expecting to receive, for their notes (excluding VAT).

rounding.nation: Each figure is rounded to two decimal places as it is added up. A total can differ by a few pence from the same figures added first and rounded once.
rounding.uk: Each figure is rounded to two decimal places as it is added up. The total can differ by a few pence from the same figures added first and rounded once.

calculation.source: The figures come from the monthly reports that operators submit, not from the summary logs that the UK waste balance uses. Where an operator has submitted a month more than once, only the latest submission counts. Quarterly reports do not count.
calculation.total: Each table ends with a Grand Total row, which adds up the figures for every material. No average price is calculated for it, so that cell shows a dash (-).
calculation.zero: Each month shows a reprocessor table and an exporter table, with every material appearing in both. A 0.00 figure displays where there’s no reported operator activity, where operators have reported, but left a figure out, and where a month has not been submitted.

completeness.nation: The figures shown are only as good as the reports submitted by the operators. Operators who have not submitted a monthly report do not contribute to the reported figures. The most recent months are less complete as reports are still being submitted. Each month shows how many of the monthly reports have been received.
completeness.uk: The figures shown are only as good as the reports submitted by the operators. Operators that have not submitted a month add nothing to the figures. The most recent months are the least complete because reports are still arriving. Each month shows how many of the monthly reports have been received.

description.england: For each month, the tables show what accredited reprocessors and exporters reported by material (tonnage received, recycled or exported, and sent on). They also show the tonnage PRNs and PERNs were issued for, the revenue from those notes and the average price for each tonne. These figures are included in the monthly redacted data workbook (XLSX).
description.nation: For each month, the tables show what accredited reprocessors and exporters reported by material (tonnage received, recycled or exported, and sent on). They also show the tonnage PRNs and PERNs were issued for, the revenue from those notes and the average price for each tonne.
description.uk: For each month, the tables show what accredited reprocessors and exporters reported by material (tonnage received, recycled or exported, or sent on). They also show the tonnage PRNs and PERNs were issued for, the revenue from those notes and the average price for each tonne. These figures are included in the monthly published (redacted) data workbook (XLSX).

fewOperators.noReport: Accredited operators count even if they have not submitted their reports or their reports add nothing to the figure.
fewOperators.total: A Grand Total is calculated for all the materials in a table column, operators accredited for more than one material still only count once. Also, an operator is a business, so only counts once regardless of however many sites it has.

marked.nation: Figures are marked ‘c’ to show that the data came from only 1 or 2 operators. Figures are also marked ‘c’ when no operators were accredited for it, but another figure in the same row holds data (for example, a late report from an operator cancelled for the whole month). Rows with no accredited operators and nothing in them are not marked ‘c’.
marked.uk: Figures are marked ‘c’ to show that the data came from only 1 or 2 operators. Rows with no accredited operators and nothing in them are not marked ‘c’.

marketInsights.heading: Reported reprocessor and exporter packaging waste data
marketInsights.linkText: View reported reprocessor and exporter packaging waste data

calculation.bands: A report is counted under the tonnage band the accreditation holds now, not the band it held in the month the report was owed. A band change therefore moves all of that accreditation’s outstanding months to the new band.
calculation.glass: Glass is two materials here. An operator accredited for glass remelt and for glass other holds a registration for each, owes a report for each, and appears in both tables.
calculation.heading: How the figures are calculated
calculation.live: The figures are live. They come from the monthly reports and the accreditations held at the time shown above, not from a record of what was published. If an operator submits a report late, its month stops being outstanding.
calculation.owed: One monthly report is owed for each accredited registration, so an operator accredited for two materials, or at two sites, owes two reports a month. A registration with no accreditation owes none, and so does one whose accreditation was never approved, whatever validity dates it carries.
calculation.source: The figures count the monthly reports accredited operators owe and have not submitted. Quarterly reports do not count.
calculation.submitted: A month counts as submitted once the operator has submitted it, whatever figures the report carries. A report the operator has started but not submitted does not count, and neither does one submitted for a month the accreditation does not owe. A report submitted and later unsubmitted still counts, because the submission is kept, so its month is not outstanding.
calculation.validity: Once an accreditation has been approved, a report is owed for every month its validity period covered any part of, so the month it started counts and so does the month it ended. A suspended accreditation still owes its reports. A cancelled one owes nothing for a month in which it is still cancelled on the last day.
calculation.zero: A cell shows 0 where nothing is outstanding, whether every report owed was submitted or no report was owed at all. Every material and every band appears for every month either way.

outstandingReturns.description: The tables show how many monthly reports accredited operators have not submitted, by material and tonnage band. Reprocessors and exporters are counted together and no operator is named. The monthly market insights workbook uses these figures.
outstandingReturns.heading: Missing monthly reports: UK

marketInsights.pageTitle: Reported reprocessor and exporter packaging waste data

calculation.columns: The columns run from January in the reporting year to the last complete month and the totals add the monthly data together.

counted.exported: an overseas reprocessor received the exported waste
counted.leadIn: The same rules apply to counted loads as apply to the operator’s own waste balance. An accreditation must be valid on the date that the load is counted. A load counts for the month that:
counted.product: a recycled product left the reprocessing site

calculation.deductions: For reprocessors accredited on the tonnage they receive, any tonnage sent on is taken off the figure in the month that the load leaves the site. It’s taken off even if the accreditation was not valid on the date it left. The figures include tonnage for PRNs and PERNs the operator has issued from its waste balance and that the operator has already issued notes for.
calculation.heading: How the table is compiled
calculation.source: The figures come from the most recent summary logs submitted for each accreditation, they do not come from monthly reports. To show how complete the data is, the last row reveals how many operators submitted a monthly report against how many reports were due.

wasteBalance.description: The table shows the tonnage included in accredited operator or exporter waste balances by material and accreditation type, less any tonnage that has been sent on. These figures are included in the monthly published (redacted) data workbook (XLSX).

table.published: Published total, without the months marked [c]

fewOperators.accredited: An operator counts as accredited for a figure if, on any day of the month, it was accredited to reprocess that material (reprocessor figures) or to export it (exporter figures). Suspended operators count, but operators whose accreditations were cancelled for the whole month do not. Accredited operators count towards the number of operators, even if none of their tonnage is included in a figure.
fewOperators.total: Row totals are counted across each month, so operators accredited across more than one month still only count once towards the number of operators. Also, an operator is a business, so only counts once regardless of however many sites it has.
fewOperators.marked: Figures are marked ‘c’ to show that the data came from only 1 or 2 operators. Figures are also marked ‘c’ when 2 accreditation types (Exp and Rep) are combined to denote that commercial confidentiality exists within a row. Rows with no accredited operators and nothing in them are not marked ‘c’.

fewOperators.heading: Figures marked ‘c’
fewOperators.key: Some shorthand is used in this table, [c] = confidential. This figure could reveal an individual operator’s own figures, because fewer than three operators were accredited for it.
fewOperators.accredited: An operator counts as accredited for a figure if, on any day of the month, it was accredited to reprocess that material (reprocessor figures) or to export it (exporter figures). Suspended operators count, but operators whose accreditations were cancelled for the whole month do not.
